---
title: "CLI options: every flag, its default, and the R argument it sets"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, results = "asis")
```

This page is generated when the site is built. Its data is the map that
`harness/tools/optiondrift.py` (LEDGER #151) checks before every test tier:
each `make_option()` of the four wrappers under `extdata/`, the exported R
function's formal it is forwarded to, and both defaults compared as values.
A row whose status is not `ok` is one of:

- `skip`: a default that is not a literal on one side (the two FlexRV
  transform specs are named constants), so it is not compared.
- `cli_only`: a flag the wrapper consumes itself and does not forward.
- `formal_only`: an argument of the R function the CLI does not expose.
- `allowed`: a divergence the owner has decided and a ledger row records.
- `drift`: an undecided divergence. The test tiers refuse to run with one,
  so a published page never shows it.

Which options are live, partly live, refused or inert is a hand-traced
question the generator cannot answer; that column is on
[the status page](cli_status.html), and the surprising flag combinations
are on [flag surprises](flag_surprises.html).

```{r load}
tool <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("DESCRIPTION")),
                  "harness", "tools", "optiondrift.py")
raw <- system2("python3", c(tool, "--json"), stdout = TRUE)
doc <- jsonlite::fromJSON(paste(raw, collapse = "\n"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
esc <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("|", "\\|", x, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub("\n", " ", x, fixed = TRUE)
}
code <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x) | x == "", "", paste0("`", esc(x), "`"))
cell <- function(v) if (is.null(v)) NA_character_ else as.character(v)
counts <- vapply(doc$wrappers, function(w) w$n_options, numeric(1))
cat(sprintf("**%d options across %d wrappers** (%s).\n\n", sum(counts),
            length(counts), paste(sprintf("%s %d", vapply(doc$wrappers,
            function(w) basename(w$wrapper), ""), counts), collapse = ", ")))
```

```{r tables}
for (w in doc$wrappers) {
  cat(sprintf("## `%s` -> `%s()`\n\n", basename(w$wrapper), w$`function`))
  cat(sprintf("Function source `%s`; reference page: [%s](../reference/%s.html).\n\n",
              w$source, w$`function`, w$`function`))
  recs <- w$records
  df <- data.frame(
    flag = vapply(recs, function(r) cell(r$flag), ""),
    type = vapply(recs, function(r) cell(r$type), ""),
    cli_default = vapply(recs, function(r) cell(r$cli_default), ""),
    argument = vapply(recs, function(r) cell(r$formal), ""),
    r_default = vapply(recs, function(r) cell(r$r_default), ""),
    status = vapply(recs, function(r) cell(r$status), ""),
    help = vapply(recs, function(r) cell(r$help), ""),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  out <- data.frame(
    Flag = ifelse(is.na(df$flag), "", paste0("`--", df$flag, "`")),
    Type = ifelse(is.na(df$type), "", df$type),
    `CLI default` = code(df$cli_default),
    `R argument` = code(df$argument),
    `R default` = code(df$r_default),
    Status = df$status,
    Help = ifelse(is.na(df$help), "", esc(df$help)),
    check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  print(knitr::kable(out, format = "markdown"))
  cat("\n\n")
  off <- df$status[!df$status %in% c("ok", "skip", "cli_only", "formal_only")]
  if (length(off)) {
    cat(sprintf("**%d row(s) not `ok`: %s.**\n\n", length(off),
                paste(sort(unique(off)), collapse = ", ")))
  }
}
```

## How the map is made

`optiondrift.py` paren-matches the `make_option(` blocks, the function's
`<- function(` signature and the wrapper's call site (`formal = opt$flag`,
`opt[["flag"]]`, or a local whose assignment mentions exactly one
`opt$flag`). Defaults are parsed as R literals and compared as values:
`1L` equals `1`, `1e-05` equals `1e-5`, a comma string equals `c(...)`,
and three coercions the readers perform are honoured (`""`/`NULL`, the
sex codes as strings or numbers, `"FALSE"`/`FALSE` for `--invNormalize`).
For step 1 the wrapper calls `fitNULLGLMM_multi`, whose `...` forwards to
`fitNULLGLMM`; both signatures are read and the multi's own win.
